name: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
subgenre: First-person tactile machinery / artillery procedure simulator
scopeFitReason: Our assessment: one compact machine, one input puzzle and a dramatic output can form a three-week vertical slice. The complete game's mission and equipment breadth cannot.
team: Two people: Nick Nieuwoudt / Nick Talmers and Dominik Latos; Steam page reports 20+ years of combined experience.
devTime: Just over one year, according to the developer interview; not a three-week production.
hook: Operate a colossal gun through physical maps, levers and machinery from inside its control room.
whyDemand: The interview links early short-video traction to tactile controls and sound; the later demo showed sustained engagement.
spin: Our hypothesis: a tiny emergency-services control room where satisfying procedures trigger absurd visible consequences. Test one machine and three escalating jobs before expanding.

observedMetrics.scope: Steam base game, all-language review total

reportedOutcome.metric: >365,000 Steam copies and $4.7m gross revenue by day five; 4% refunds

marketingEvents.date: Before June 2026 demo; exact dates not disclosed
marketingEvents.result: >400k wishlists before demo; no isolated channel attribution

marketingEvents.action: Playable demo backed by prior audience

caveat: A successful experienced team, not a typical outcome. PVKK is an acknowledged inspiration. Gross revenue is not developer profit or organic-attributed revenue.

name: Guildrun
releaseDate: To be announced on Steam; July 2026 interview targeted first half of 2027
tropes: PvP format reworked for solo play
scopeFitReason: Our assessment: a six-unit, one-arena synergy prototype fits three weeks; matching the released demo's content, balance and UI quality does not.
team: Leyline: six full-time people alongside two founders, freelancers and outreach support, per the interview; partly grant-funded.
devTime: Full production duration not disclosed. Community tests began December 2025; weekly alpha iteration from January 2026.
hook: Build absurdly powerful autochess teams without queues, time pressure or a PvP meta.
whyDemand: Players asking for PvE autochess became an initial target; specialist long-form creators reached this systems-focused audience.
spin: Our hypothesis: a comic workplace autobattler with six readable employee archetypes and one dramatic rule-breaking synergy. Validate replay interest, not just clip views.

marketingEvents.result: Developer says organic coverage exceeded paid floor; short-form was not a major driver

name: Hearth and Hamlet
subgenre: Finite city-themed clicker / idle resource progression
scopeFitReason: Our assessment: one authored diorama, three resources and a short upgrade tree are feasible. Scope out free placement, deep city simulation and large content trees.
team: Solo Australian developer at Phorust Studios, also working as a teacher; publishers Runic Forge and Gamersky Games.
devTime: Not disclosed in accessible interview; began as a classroom incremental project.
hook: Watch a tiny settlement visibly grow through accessible upgrades and resource accumulation.
whyDemand: Strong launch intent and long median playtime support finite progression demand; mismatched city-building expectations also created negative reviews.
spin: Our hypothesis: a visually escalating miniature workplace that becomes comically over-automated. Make each unlock alter the diorama, and show the fixed-layout rule upfront.

hook: Explore together when talking, gesturing and miscommunication are the actual mechanics.
whyDemand: GDCo estimates show strong overlap with PEAK and Lethal Company, supporting a social audience beyond the developer's previous game.
spin: Our hypothesis: a short office escape where each colleague loses a different communication channel. Build one cooperative puzzle with funny misunderstandings, not an open world.

name: Dear Passengers
mode: Online co-op; Steam also lists single-player
scopeFitReason: Our assessment: flight, loose-object physics and replicated co-op multiply risk. A stationary cabin with scripted turbulence is a realistic three-week slice only with an existing networking stack.
team: FLEXUS: roughly 70-person studio according to Alinea; this game's dedicated team size is not disclosed.
devTime: Not disclosed in the accessible source; studio has prior mobile development experience.
hook: Run a failing airline together as passengers, luggage and disasters collide inside the plane.
whyDemand: Alinea reports >1m wishlists and strong overlap with existing co-op buyers; the familiar job plus absurd failure is easy to understand in a clip.
spin: Our hypothesis: crew a disastrous cruise buffet or hotel elevator with one shared fragile objective. Preserve cascading blame but change the task, environment and interaction language.
